cand.title: Second Annual University of Toronto Obstetric Anesthesia Conference
cand.organizationName: Temerty Faculty of Medicine, University of Toronto
cand.excerpt: CME-accredited, one-day medical-education conference on October 3, 2026, with an explicitly described audience of more than 100 clinicians and decision-makers from across Canada. The organizer advertises preferred hotel rates for out-of-town attendees, making lodging demand directly evidenced, while the conference format supports food-and-beverage and meeting-related demand.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Ronald George, Head of Obstetrical Anesthesia at Mount Sinai Hospital, is the strongest named relationship contact: he personally promotes the 2026 programme as “our program” and describes the CAS partnership. His hotel-contract authority is not established. MacKenzie Ellis is publicly listed as Sinai Health CME Coordinator for another 2026 conference; this is a relevant administrative referral candidate, not a verified buyer or confirmed coordinator for this anesthesia conference. No second event-specific lodging decision-maker was verified.
findings.futureEdition: No next edition officially announced was found for December 2026–June 2028. Upcoming dates, city and venue remain null. The October 3, 2026 edition is past; the registration page says “Event ended.” “Second Annual” supports recurrence intent, not an announced 2027 date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: a 157-room city hotel could serve a modest subset of travelling delegates, faculty or VIPs, rather than require an exclusive hotel takeover. The advertised audience of over 100 is not overnight demand and supplies no basis for a room-block estimate. Hospital-based education favours a city-hotel proposition rather than a resort. Harbourfront is not the documented hospital venue location; MTCC walkability adds no event-specific advantage. Side meetings or receptions are proposals only, with no sourced demand; do not promise catering until restaurant/lounge and banquet operations are verified.
findings.venueCommitments: The 2026 advertised venue was Women’s College Hospital, 76 Grenville Street, Toronto, ON M5S 1B2: Toronto proper, downtown hospital district, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. It is a hospital, not a competing hotel. No room/auditorium within the hospital was identified. This is a historical venue commitment only; no future venue commitment was found.
findings.historicalRotation: October 25, 2025: Ben Sadowski Auditorium, Mount Sinai Hospital, 600 University Avenue, 18th Floor, Toronto. October 3, 2026: Women’s College Hospital, 76 Grenville Street, Toronto. These establish a local venue change, not destination rotation. Official 2025 material describes a return after a five-year break; an older departmental account says the conference had been offered at Mount Sinai since 2003 and paused in 2020–2021. Do not interpret “Second Annual” as the second edition in the entire historical series or project uninterrupted annual recurrence.
findings.accommodationSourcing: 2026 edition-specific preferred-rate hotel: Chelsea Hotel, Toronto — the only hotel named in the reviewed edition materials. Exact organizer wording: “Travelling from out of town? We are pleased to offer preferred rates at the Chelsea Hotel, Toronto. To reserve, please visit chelseatoronto.com or call the hotel and use the booking code: MMOSI.” This is direct attendee booking through the hotel using a code. It evidences an incumbent preferred-rate arrangement, not a disclosed guaranteed room block, exclusive housing contract or open inventory. No published allocation, rate amount, cutoff, room nights, housing bureau, PCO or open hotel RFP was identified. Future sourcing remains unconfirmed.
findings.organizationStructure: Academic/hospital-led medical education: the Mount Sinai Anesthesia Department is identified as host/organizer in event listings; University of Toronto’s Temerty Faculty of Medicine and Department of Anesthesiology and Pain Medicine publish the programme. The Canadian Anesthesiologists’ Society OB Section is an explicit collaborator, not proven hotel buyer. Women’s College Hospital is the 2026 venue; Chelsea Hotel is the preferred lodging provider. Eventbrite is the ticketing channel. No external PCO, agency or DMC was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Chelsea already had an edition-specific preferred-rate offer for 2026. Its own location information places it 700 m from Women’s College Hospital, a practical convenience advantage over a Harbourfront proposition (comparative suitability is inference, not measured Radisson travel time). No sold-out hotel, displaced delegates, unmet room demand, overflow request or exclusivity was evidenced. Do not present Chelsea’s generic hospital rate as the conference agreement; the university event page separately establishes the conference offer.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Ronald George through his official university profile to ask who manages conference logistics and accommodation, whether another edition is planned, and when any hotel arrangement will be reviewed. Request actual 2026 out-of-town attendance, Chelsea pickup/room nights, faculty lodging and unmet needs before sizing an offer. If redirected, ask Sinai Health CME Coordinator MacKenzie Ellis to identify the correct administrator; do not assume she owns this event. Offer a contingent supplemental lodging proposal only after dates, venue and sourcing access are confirmed; verify hotel catering capability before discussing hosted functions.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: Closed historical cycle: October 3, 2026 has passed and ticketing says “Event ended.” Neither lodging nor conference-venue revenue for that edition is a current sales opportunity. Published Chelsea preferred rates do not prove all attendees stayed there, but no accessible residual demand is evidenced.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Conditional inference only: verified 2025 and 2026 editions and explicit out-of-town preferred-rate marketing justify a relationship-development approach for a possible later cycle. A future Toronto edition, lodging tender, alternative-hotel need and planner willingness to use Harbourfront remain unconfirmed. Seek supplemental speaker/delegate lodging only if requested; do not claim overflow or an open RFP.

remainingUncertainties: No officially published next-edition dates, city or venue were found within December 2026–June 2028.
Actual 2026 attendance, non-local share, overnight stays, peak rooms, room nights and Chelsea pickup are unpublished in reviewed materials.

Future hospital-versus-hotel venue flexibility and any off-site meeting/reception demand are unknown.
